scope.scopeRationale: Single certified product line and one documented OfficeEMR EHI export stack: KnowledgeOwl /ehi-export article plus ZIP artifacts (schemas, data dictionary, sample export) and screenshots.
scope._includedProducts: Used product research and CHPL record (product name OfficeEMR, CHPL ID 10914, certification 2022-06-06) and confirmed all OfficeEMR-specific evidence points to the same family in the same support portal.
scope._excludedProducts: No other named OfficeEMR-branded modules were documented in the collected sources; specialty add-on products (e.g., ENTChoice) are integrations within the same platform and are not separate EHI documentation streams in this workspace.
scope._versionsInScope: Kept scope to the OfficeEMR 21 (2021) CHPL product plus artifacts dated 2023, plus the 2025-12-19 KnowledgeOwl page revision from which those files are linked; did not include legacy InfoDive (separate Data Export) pages unrelated to b(10).
scope.scopeNotes: Primary question is native multi-file EHI export completeness against OfficeEMR-stored clinical and administrative data; API-only g(10) artifacts were excluded unless referenced by the EHI export documentation.
scope._scopeNotes: Evidence first comes from the registered URL and directly linked artifacts; alternate systems (legacy InfoDive CSV export, FHIR portal links) were explicitly treated as separate workflows.

items.relevance: Confirms the evidence path starts from https://officeemr.knowledgeowl.com/help/ehi-export and that documentation is public and directly downloadable.

assessmentFlow.method: Collected all linked artifacts from the registered URL and validated them against downloaded ZIP/PDF files under results/isalus-healthcare/downloads.
observations: Discovery succeeded with no auth barriers and no dead links for core artifacts.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Allows deterministic scope boundary and avoids reliance on marketing pages or external standards docs.

items.relevance: Direct evidence that OfficeEMR ships a dedicated b10 entity model spanning clinical and PM domains rather than only USCDI-only resources.
Confirms that OfficeEMR includes PM, scheduling, portal, and specialty workflows, useful to judge expected export surface.

gaps: Research does not enumerate every possible internal entity in the product workflow.

assessmentFlow.method: Mapped product capabilities from research (EHR + PM + billing + communication + modules) to the domains listed in the EHI export artifacts.
observations: Model appears broader than classic clinical-only EHR profiles due to integrated PM and workflow content.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Raises expected baseline for export breadth beyond ambulatory core clinical records.

items.relevance: Shows payload shape: per-entity JSON arrays per file plus readme.json and no indication of API-only response envelope.
Confirms field-level naming and human-readable descriptions alongside schema types.
Demonstrates explicit coverage intent for claims, appointments, demographics, communications, and specialty entities.

gaps: Value sets and value-level enumerations are not present in visible dictionaries.

assessmentFlow.method: Classified actual export mechanism and format from live artifacts: one file per entity in multi-file bundle JSON with schema and sample support docs.
observations: Format is vendor-native JSON, not FHIR or CCDA for core clinical payloads.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Positions OfficeEMR as a true native export implementation with practical recomposition advantages but mapping requirements for consumers.

items.relevance: Sample contains 58 files while schema list is 81 files, indicating sparse coverage in the sample dataset but not necessarily missing definitions.
Upcoming additions suggest evolving field coverage and reinforce that release completeness is snapshot-dependent.

gaps: No full-practice export sample available to confirm all entity population behavior.

assessmentFlow.method: Contrasted documented schema breadth with the single-patient sample and supporting text about bulk export handoff process.
observations: Most core clinical/PM domains appear represented; some high-priority specialties and workflows may be only sparsely represented in sample.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Supports conservative scoring with explicit uncertainty on edge-case and low-frequency domains.

items.relevance: Field-level schema and concrete output together make reconstruction feasible despite lack of semantic enums.

assessmentFlow.method: Applied schema depth, self-service access, mapping risk, and domain-level completeness checks with conservative penalties for undocumented values and missing edge-case validation.
observations: OfficeEMR export is broad and machine-readable, but some areas are explicitly undocumented at code/value granularity and not verifiable from single-patient sample.
assessmentFlow.impactOnAssessment: Final result is high coverage with moderate confidence and explicit caveats on edge workflows and rare entities.

items.relevance: Confirms native multi-file JSON packaging and patient-specific payload structure.
Shows machine-readable schema coverage across entities.

gaps: No machine-readable value sets for coded fields are in the schema set.

exportSurface.accessibilityNotes: Single-patient export appears self-serve via role-gated UI and immediate ZIP retrieval; all-patient export requires team submission and a team-processing delay (~15 days).
exportSurface._container: Used Evidence from sample export and artifact layout; export is not bundled as single file or API payload and is not a DB dump. Chosen as multi_file_bundle because each domain is a separate JSON file.
exportSurface._formats: Primary payload uses JSON arrays per file. The supporting documentation PDF is non-machine-readable, but not the actual export format.
exportSurface._standardProfile: No FHIR/CCDA standard profile for the payload; no external clinical profile references in schema file names or sample layout.
exportSurface._selfService: Single-patient path is clearly self-service. Bulk path includes vendor-assisted processing with lead time, so overall export mechanism is not fully self-service.
exportSurface._operationalBurden: Single-patient retrieval is low burden (self-serve). Bulk adds administrative overhead and wait time, producing an overall medium burden classification.

items.relevance: Supports mostly direct mapping from source table structures.
Provides names and descriptions that reduce guesswork, despite missing semantic domains for enumerations.

gaps: Limited formal relationship graph and no published constraints for cross-field cardinalities.

lossOrConflationExamples: Without value-set codebooks, many coded strings in sample retain meaning only by implementation convention.
Some template-derived clinical structures rely on nested sub-files; consumers need explicit join logic across encounter-related entities.
suspectedOmissions: No dedicated schema for intelligent intake forms, RPM streams, telehealth session metadata, or fax activity.

items.relevance: Core patient identity and contact fields appear in both schema and sample payload.

domainAssessments.rationale: Demographic identity, address, communication and identifier fields are clearly present, with field names and descriptions documented.
caveats: Date format conventions are mixed across payloads and not consistently documented in one canonical section.

items.relevance: Multiple finance/coverage files exist with sample records and schema descriptions.

domainAssessments.rationale: Claims, claim procedures, denials, payments, eligibility, price estimates, statements, and prior authorizations are represented.
caveats: Some financial extensions (e.g., sliding_fee, fee_schedule) are schema-defined but absent in the single-patient sample.
No separate claims adjudication workflow traces are provided.

items.relevance: Core diagnosis/problem tables and notes appear in both schema and sample.

domainAssessments.rationale: Problem list and related annotations are explicitly exported in dedicated files.

items.relevance: Medication fields are shown with prescription, history, and eRx-related links in product context.

gaps: Sample shows limited medication breadth and does not validate all prescription detail variants.

domainAssessments.rationale: Medication and pharmacy-related entities are present, but coverage depth for all prescription states is not observable from one sample patient.

items.relevance: Fine-grained vital fields documented and sample-recorded.

domainAssessments.rationale: Vitals are explicitly modeled and included with extensive fields in schema and sample.
caveats: Date/time fields are inconsistently formatted in examples (string variants).

items.relevance: Clinical note and template encounter files are present for encounter-based narrative workflows.

gaps: Evidence of all encounter template variants and specialties is partial in sample.

domainAssessments.rationale: Core note types and template fragments exist, supporting reconstructable encounter documentation.
caveats: Custom template and specialist note variants may be stored in ways not directly visible in one sample.

items.relevance: Both files are present in schema and sample; HTI-1 updates mention planned allergy verification extensions.

gaps: Planned HTI-1 additions show current schema may not yet include verification fields for some allergy entries.

domainAssessments.rationale: Allergy entities are defined and populated in sample; upcoming additions imply incremental enhancement rather than missing core capture.

items.relevance: Document metadata and cross-references for images are present with dedicated schema and sample files.

gaps: Binary image payloads are not included in export artifact evidence here.

domainAssessments.rationale: Metadata for documents/images is included, but consumers need external object retrieval for actual content when present.
caveats: Binary attachments may require separate retrieval assumptions not documented in schema.

items.relevance: Laboratory and immunization objects are schema-defined and present in sample.

domainAssessments.rationale: Core lab/immunization/order records exist; order fulfillment depth and cross-file result relationships are implicit rather than formally constrained.
caveats: No explicit relationship graph was found.

items.relevance: Portal and communication-related entities appear in schema, and feature set includes patient messaging workflows.

gaps: No dedicated portal analytics/event logs were found.

domainAssessments.rationale: Communication recipient/message and comment entities exist, but not full usage/audit context from patient portal modules.

items.locator: product-research + absence in data entity list
items.relevance: Product features include telehealth and tele-intake modules, but no corresponding sample/schema entities were confirmed as dedicated entities.

gaps: No specific telehealth or intake-form entity was named in schema sample names.

domainAssessments.rationale: Evidence suggests these workflows exist in product UX but do not have explicit standalone exported entities in the captured artifact set.
caveats: These records may be represented indirectly through template encounter or note entities, but that is unverified.
